children: Jet fuel demand in the U.S., as well as production, remained stable for the week ended Friday, according to the latest round of Energy Information Administration data. Stockpiles, though, saw an increase.
Demand for jet fuel in the U.S. shifted down 18,000 b/d to 1.754 million b/d. That's about 26,000 b/d below the four-week average, but some 50,000 b/d over year-ago marks.
Production of jet fuel was also stable during the week. Overall U.S. production was up just 5,000 b/d to 2.03 million b/d.
Regionally, jet fuel output was also stable.

The biggest mover was in the Midwest (PADD 2) where jet fuel production was up 7,000 b/d to 362,000 b/d. Gulf Coast (PADD 3) production also rose, gaining a meager 4,000 b/d to 1.095 million b/d - the second week in a row where regional output has been under 1.1 million b/d.
Meanwhile, both East Coast (PADD 1) and West Coast (PADD 5) production levels shaved off a little bit, dropping 3,000 b/d to 63,000 b/d and down 1,000 b/d to 474,000 b/d, respectively.
While demand and production were flat, stockpiles of jet fuel rose on the week.
Overall national jet fuel inventories were up 180,000 bbl to 45.873 million bbl. That's the second consecutive week below the 46-million-bbl mark.

Regionally, most areas in the country saw increases in inventories. PADD 1 stocks were up 273,000 bbl to 11.329 million bbl. PADD 5 jet fuel inventories saw a similar build, rising 255,000 bbl to 11.371 million bbl. PADD 2 stocks of jet fuel rose to 8.212 million bbl after a rise of 145,000 bbl.
On the other hand, PADD 3 stockpiles of jet fuel dropped 515,000 bbl to 14.304 million bbl, the lowest level in the area since the week ended May 29.
